title: More than half of heroin/morphine misuse death hotspots in England and Wales are seaside locations
meta_description: Six of the 10 towns and cities in England and Wales with the highest rates of heroin/morphine-misuse1 deaths are coastal holiday resorts.

breadcrumb.text: More than half of heroin/morphine misuse death hotspots in England and Wales are seaside locations

lede: Some of England and Wales's favourite seaside resort areas are now among the towns with the highest rates of deaths from the misuse of heroin/morphine.

body.h3: Drug misuse deaths likely to be tied to deprivation
body.text: Public Health England has suggested a link between areas of higher deprivation and drugs misuse.

body.h3: Drug misuse deaths likely to be tied to deprivation
body.text: Their report, [Preventing Drugs Misuse Deaths](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/health-matters-preventing-drug-misuse-deaths/health-matters-preventing-drug-misuse-deaths), said: “Social factors, including housing, employment and deprivation, are associated with substance misuse and these social factors moderate drug treatment outcomes.”

body.h3: Drug misuse deaths likely to be tied to deprivation
body.text: The Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs linked an increase in heroin misuse deaths to the “deepening socio-economic deprivation since the financial crisis of 2008” in its publication [Reducing Opioid-Related Deaths in the UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/576560/ACMD-Drug-Related-Deaths-Report-161212.pdf).

body.h3: How heroin and morphine deaths have varied over time
body.text: There were 3,744 drug poisoning deaths (involving both legal and illegal drugs) registered in 2016 in England and Wales. Of those deaths, 2,593 were from drug misuse, which represents 69% of total deaths. In 1993 the proportion was 38%.

body.h3: How heroin and morphine deaths have varied over time
body.text: Heroin and/or morphine is the drug used by the so-called “[Trainspotting generation](https://www.theguardian.com/society/2017/aug/02/trainspotting-generation-most-likely-to-die-from-drug-misuse)”. Death rates from the misuse of opiates have [steadily climbed](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/deaths/articles/deathsinvolvingheroinupbytwothirdsintwoyears/2015-09-03) between 1993 (when data were first collected) and 1996; since then they have plateaued at around 80% of all opiate deaths, through to 2016.

body.h3: How heroin and morphine deaths have varied over time
body.text: This “Trainspotting generation”, which became addicted to heroin in the 1980s and 1990s, has been cited as one of the reasons for the increase. This may also explain why the highest rate of death from drugs misuse in 2016 was among the 40 to 49-year-olds, overtaking those aged 30 to 39 years.

body.h3: How heroin and morphine deaths have varied over time
body.text: In 2016, the number of drug-related deaths where heroin and/or morphine were mentioned on the death certificate has increased by almost eight times since 1993. There has been only a slight increase from 2015, where 1,201 deaths were registered, but there has been an increase of almost two-thirds since 2012, following the “[heroin drought](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/deaths/bulletins/deathsrelatedtodrugpoisoninginenglandandwales/2015registrations#deaths-involving-heroin-andor-morphine-doubled-in-the-last-3-years-and-are-now-the-highest-on-record)” of 2010 to 2011.
